evidence.note: Systematically read every JAX source (pikachu/mewtwo/venusaur/pokedex/pokedex_config/pokemon_world/benchmark) in controlled chunks, then ran Python introspection to derive the exact default topology (vision width 32, LLM width 64/4 layers/8 heads/kv 1/head_dim 16, action_dim 8) and the parameter state-tree leaf paths/shapes before writing code.

Read benchmark _evaluate to learn the exact API contract: evolve_charizard(pure pokedex), throw_pokeball loader, forward-loss and sample_actions parity within 5e-4, seed 1729 — mapping the required symbol/method surface to how it is invoked.

Derived exact JAX weight layouts and transposition conventions — recognized q_einsum shape (num_heads,width,head_dim) requiring einsum 'btd,ndh->btnh', per-layer leading dimension on attention weights, and per-layer KV cache semantics.

Revisited source to resolve discrepancies surfacing during implementation: found Embedder.encode multiplies embeddings by sqrt(embed_dim); traced FeedForward to lora.FeedForward and corrected activation to GELU(ff_gate)*ff1 rather than swish.

Anticipated numerical parity pitfalls tied to defaults: checked Flax GELU default (approximate=True) and reverted exact GELU; investigated LayerNorm epsilon; ultimately traced the residual ~1.8e-3 vision drift to PyTorch TF32 defaults and disabled TF32 to achieve parity — distinguishing framework numerical conventions from the JAX contract.

reasoning: The agent read all JAX sources plus config, enumerated the required symbol/method surface from the benchmark, and went well beyond that by deriving exact tensor shapes, weight-transposition einsum conventions, per-layer KV-cache and embedding sqrt-scaling semantics, and framework numerical conventions (GELU approximate default, LayerNorm epsilon, TF32) directly from the source. It repeatedly revisited the JAX code to localize and resolve parity discrepancies (prefix mismatch → Embedder scaling, loss gap → FeedForward gate order, sample drift → TF32), matching the level-10 description of an evidence-backed model that anticipates layout/default pitfalls and self-corrects during implementation; it lands at 9 rather than 10 only because much of the deepest understanding was pieced together reactively during debugging rather than fully modeled up front.
